I'm an incoming grade 12 po and our school (which is private) was part of the pilot implementation of the strengthened curriculum.

 I can say that it is lightweight and true to its claim as per this video intended to say. Also, yung pag pili ng electives, we had the chance to pick two before magkaron ng official classes pero hindi na sunod. Idk if may say ba ang DepEd sa scenario na to, but as a student na want magkaron ng security sa future—I chose the electives from TechVoc para sana sa NC2 kaso nauwi sa wala. We didn't know why hindi natuloy, walang explanation samin kaya super disappointed talaga kami. 

But as we reached the end of the academic year, I can say that it was definitely more tolerable than the last senior high years. We get to focus more on what we should know, GENERALLY before mag-college. 


Now, I want to know what changes would DepEd do again? People, including me. Wants to know about sa kumakalat na balita about 95% would be the average of an honor student. Isn't that too high? well personally, I am a academic achiever, I think DepEd wanted to make the students try harder than what they usually do. Pero sana ma-consider nyo na Firstly, hindi lahat nakaka-akyat sa 90. Secondly, hindi basehan ang numero kung ano yung matutunan ng isang tao. At this point, if I-implement nyo yan ng walang proper survey studying would only serve as ranking nalang to have honors at hindi na para mag aral e.

I have a theory - I feel like children need more of the tactile in the beginning of their learning because their minds can't handle the theoretical yet. The screen behaves like a window, a barrier,  which the child needs to navigate through. We are trying to get their "prefrontal cortex"/reasoning mind working... Handwriting forces the child to evaluate each word in the problems and solutions. Long hand is the way to go!
I think that screens get their "intuitive" part of their brain going which at this is age is going at 100% but what we need to do is get that other side of the brain running and integrated.  I feel like the computer can be incorporated in learning later on, when they're capable of doing algebra/geometry (a sign their prefrontal cortex can "handle" it). Just my 2 cents from experience and observation.
